text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Dense fog has paralysed traffic in Istanbul and other parts of the country over the past few days.
- Civil servants demand higher wage rises after the government awards the armed forces an average 72 percent pay increase in the new year.
- Eighty-six rebel Kurds have been killed so far in three-day cross-border operation into northern Iraq.
- Tax evaders will have an easy 1997 after the six-month- old government failed to implement overdue tax reforms.
- A human rights grouping says government troops are forcing locals to take up arms against rebel Kurds in the southeastern tosn of Lice.
- A parliamentary commission will this month discuss what to do about the government's sluggish privatisation programme.
- Two months after a scandal broke out over state ties with the underworld, not one suspect has been brought to trial and hopes of any progress against organised crime are fading fast.
- The head of a parliamentary commission set up to probe state-underworld ties says even the highest security figures are obliged to undergo questioning by their MPs.
